sara_support: Heads up — ACME reported a sudden embeddings throughput drop this morning. tokens/sec stayed flat but vectors/sec dropped by ~60% starting ~09:10 UTC. They also saw intermittent auth 429s. Customer says search latency spiked.

acme_prod_owner: yep, big impact for us. we get 429s mixed with longer tail latencies. queue depth in our telemetry spikes. billing dashboard shows a few retry bursts — could that be related?

sara_support: Reproduced quickly on our side with their payload shape. When concurrency >4 and batch_size=1 we saw 429s after ~30s of steady QPS. Snippet we used:
```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["..."]}'
```
ran in a tight loop.

mike_infra: Initial look: the 429s look like API key rate-limit hits on the embedding route (per-key window). tokens/sec staying steady suggests tokenizer side unaffected. Need to check gateway per-route quotas + any recent rate-limit config changes.

olga_sre: GPU host gpu-12 shows queue depth increase (avg +18) but GPU util ~72% — weird. That usually indicates smaller batch sizes leading to inefficient utilization, not raw saturation. Could be batching/window shrink + many tiny requests.

jonathan_eng: Also consider KV cache behavior — if client churns prefixes/inputs you can get cache misses that inflate per-request overhead. Small batches + KV misses -> vectors/sec falls even if tokens/sec looks okay. Any change in client batching recently?

acme_prod_owner: we did roll out a client change to send results immediately (batch_size=1) to reduce latency for single-item searches. We can revert if that's the culprit.

mike_infra: There's an interesting correlation: during the same window autoscaler removed a few nodes (scale-down) after a short idle period. That churn + small batches could increase head-of-line wait and cause retry storms when auth fails -> queue pileup. Also saw a couple of 502s from fallback model during the window.

sara_support: Repro steps for engineering: run the curl loop above at 10 qps, compare batch_size=1 vs batch_size=8. Collect /metrics vecs/sec and embedding_queue_depth. Observe: batch_size=1 -> vectors/sec drops; batch_size=8 -> vectors/sec returns to baseline.

olga_sre: Quick mitigations we tried: 1) pin ACME to open-embed-1 v1.2 (avoid fallback churn) 2) relax per-key rate limit temporarily for their key 3) request client to revert to batch_size >=4. After applying 1+3 on canary we saw vectors/sec back to expected and no 429s. :thumbsup:

deploybot: rollout note: pinned route for acme-prod-key -> model open-embed-1@v1.2 on canary (3 nodes). Observed no 429s during the 15m canary window. Rolling to stable now.

acme_prod_owner: Confirmed after pin + revert to batch_size=8 our vectors throughput returned to baseline and search latency improved. Thanks for the quick help.

jonathan_eng: Root cause hypothesis: client change (batch_size=1) + autoscaler scale-down churn -> many small batches + KV cache cold starts -> higher per-request overhead. Meanwhile token service rate-limit retries (429s) amplified queue head-of-line blocking, making effective vectors/sec fall. We'll validate by looking at per-key rate-limit counters and KV cache miss rate.

mike_infra: Action items: 1) alert on vectors/sec / tokens/sec ratio drop 2) surface per-key rate-limit counters in support console 3) tweak autoscaler to be conservative for routes with high vector QPS 4) add client guidance: prefer batch_size >=4 for embeddings to reduce unit cost and improve throughput.

sara_support: I documented repro steps and workaround in the support ticket and shared the quick mitigation with ACME. Will coordinate postmortem with infra/eng. Closing after follow-up PM doc is published.

olga_sre: I'll dump the GPU queue and KV cache histograms to the PM doc and include example Grafana queries.

mike_infra: Thanks team. Follow-up: let's check billing flags next week to see if rate-limit thresholds need adjustment for high-throughput customers.

acme_prod_owner: Appreciated — happy to help with any traces or payloads.

sara_support: :white_check_mark: closing this Slack thread, continuing postmortem offline.
